jsonld.site_description: Find every civic district that covers a point or address in Georgia, and who represents you there.
jsonld.app_description: Click any point in Georgia, or search an address, to see every civic district that contains it, and who represents you there — county, Georgia Senate, Georgia House and U.S. House districts, census county divisions, cities and towns, school districts and ZIP codes.
jsonld.keywords: Georgia district map, what district am I in, Georgia Senate district, Georgia House district, Georgia congressional district, Georgia county, Georgia school district lookup

brand.tagline: Every civic district that covers your point in Georgia, and who represents you there.

layers.label: U.S. House
layers.rank_note: 14 congressional districts — the largest districts Georgia carries below the state itself

source.answers: The U.S. House district covering the point, and the representative holding it.

boundary.label: Georgia General Assembly, Legislative and Congressional Reapportionment Office — the shapefile of the congressional plan passed on 7 December 2023 (Senate Bill 3EX), pre-built for the state and shipped with the app; 14 features, measured 2026-10-29. THE GENERAL ASSEMBLY'S OWN FILE: Georgia's plans are drawn on the 2020 census's geography, and the Census Bureau's current congressional map (TIGERweb Legislative layers 0 and 4, which agree for Georgia) is the same plan. The 2023 map is the one the 3 November 2026 election uses. Simplified by Douglas-Peucker at a 5 m interval and refused over an 8 m fidelity ceiling.

source.people: congress-roster.json, rebuilt weekly by CI from the public-domain unitedstates/congress-legislators dataset — including each member's district office and Washington office.

layers.label: Georgia Senate District
layers.rank_note: 56 Senate districts — larger on average than a county, smaller than a congressional district

source.answers: The Georgia Senate district covering the point, and the senator holding it.

boundary.label: Georgia General Assembly, Legislative and Congressional Reapportionment Office — the shapefile of the Senate plan passed on 5 December 2023 (Senate Bill 1EX), pre-built for the state and shipped with the app; 56 features, measured 2026-10-29. THE GENERAL ASSEMBLY'S OWN FILE AND NOT THE CENSUS BUREAU'S: Georgia's 2023 act defines its districts on the 2020 census's geography, and the Census Bureau's current edition of the county line between Lumpkin and Union counties has since moved, which moves part of two districts' ground on its map and not in law. Simplified by Douglas-Peucker at a 5 m interval and refused over an 8 m fidelity ceiling.

source.people: ga-senate-members.json, rebuilt weekly by CI from the General Assembly's own member data, the feed its member pages read: each senator's name, party, Capitol office and its telephone, e-mail address and member page. The feed also carries a district address and, for some members, a home or cell telephone, which the member pages do not show and this app does not read. A vacant seat carries a record saying so.

layers.label: County
layers.rank_note: 159 counties, pre-built from TIGERweb; the instance's offline anchor layer

boundary.label: U.S. Census TIGERweb — State_County, layer 1, pre-built for the state and shipped with the app; 159 features, measured 2026-10-29. Simplified by Douglas-Peucker at a 5 m interval and refused over an 8 m fidelity ceiling.

source.people: ga-county-officials.json, rebuilt weekly by CI from the Georgia Secretary of State's official election results, which carry county races from November 2024 on. Each commission seat on a ballot since then is named for the winner of its newest election who has taken office, and a winner not yet in office is named apart. No state office publishes who sits on the commissions. A seat last filled before November 2024 and not on a ballot since is not listed, and nobody appointed to fill a vacancy is shown — recorded as gap ga-county-commission-members.

layers.label: Georgia House District
layers.rank_note: 180 House districts — smaller on average than a county, about the size of a school district

source.answers: The Georgia House district covering the point, and the representative holding it.

boundary.label: Georgia General Assembly, Legislative and Congressional Reapportionment Office — the shapefile of the House plan passed on 5 December 2023 (House Bill 1EX), pre-built for the state and shipped with the app; 180 features, measured 2026-10-29. The General Assembly's own file rather than the Census Bureau's, for the reason the Senate layer gives. Simplified by Douglas-Peucker at a 5 m interval and refused over an 8 m fidelity ceiling.

source.people: ga-house-members.json, rebuilt weekly by CI from the General Assembly's own member data, on the same terms as the Senate's.

layers.label: School District
layers.rank_note: 181 unified districts, about 822 km2 of land on average, live from TIGERweb (no data/app file); they cover all of Georgia but Fort Benning

source.answers: The public school district covering the point.

boundary.label: U.S. Census TIGERweb — School, layer 0 (unified school districts), queried live at runtime; 181 features for Georgia, measured 2026-10-29: the 159 county school systems, the city school systems and the Fort Stewart schools.

source.people: ga-county-officials.json, from the same election results as the County card, names the board of education of each of the 159 county school systems on the same terms. The boards of the 21 city school systems are not named yet, and the state's election results do not cover the schools on Fort Stewart, the Army post — recorded as gap ga-school-board-members.
source.applies: Georgia — everywhere but Fort Benning. Measured 2026-10-29, the unified districts' Census land areas sum to 148,806 km2, and the Census's one elementary district (Fort Benning Schools, kindergarten to grade 8) adds 682 km2 to exactly the 159 counties' 149,488 km2; its two secondary districts split the same ground between the Chattahoochee and Muscogee county systems for grades 9 to 12. Those three are not drawn, and the card says so on the post.

layers.label: Census County Division
layers.rank_note: 586 census county divisions tiling the state, about 255 km2 of land on average, live from TIGERweb (no data/app file)

source.answers: The census county division containing the point and its county.

boundary.label: U.S. Census TIGERweb — Places_CouSub_ConCity_SubMCD, layer 1 (county subdivisions), queried live at runtime; 586 features for Georgia, measured 2026-10-29, every one a census county division (LSADC 22, FUNCSTAT S): an area the Census Bureau draws to report its counts.

source.people: NO OFFICEHOLDER, AND NONE IS MISSING: Georgia has no township governments, and nobody is elected from a census county division. The card says so.

layers.label: ZIP Code
layers.rank_note: 1,202 ZIP Code Tabulation Areas in the state's own bounding box, about 196 km2 of land on average, fetched live by envelope; the layer hides outside Georgia

source.answers: The ZIP Code Tabulation Area covering the point — the Census Bureau's areal approximation of the USPS delivery routes sharing a ZIP code, not a postal boundary.

boundary.label: U.S. Census TIGERweb — ZIP Code Tabulation Areas, layer 11 of the PUMA/TAD/TAZ/UGA/ZCTA service, queried live at runtime. ZCTAs carry NO STATE FIELD because they cross state lines, so this is the one TIGERweb layer here fetched by a bounding ENVELOPE rather than STATE='13'. 1,202 features in Georgia's box, measured 2026-10-29.

source.people: NO OFFICEHOLDER, AND NONE IS MISSING: a ZIP code is a mail-routing convenience, not a unit of government, so nobody is elected from one. The card says what the boundary actually is rather than leaving a reader to assume it means more.
source.applies: Georgia. The layer is hidden outside the state outline, because outside it the Census's point query answers with a neighbouring state's real ZIP code (Phenix City, Alabama gives 36867 and North Augusta, South Carolina 29841, measured 2026-10-29).

layers.label: City or Town
layers.rank_note: 538 incorporated places, about 26 km2 of land on average, live from TIGERweb (no data/app file)

source.answers: The city or town containing the point, if any, and whether it is one government with its county.

boundary.label: U.S. Census TIGERweb — Places_CouSub_ConCity_SubMCD, layer 4 (incorporated places), queried live at runtime; 538 features for Georgia, measured 2026-10-29: 430 cities, 101 towns and the places the Census files for the governments a city and its county share — Athens-Clarke County, Augusta-Richmond County, Macon-Bibb County, Cusseta-Chattahoochee County, Georgetown-Quitman County, Webster County and Echols County — with Columbus, one government with Muscogee County, filed as a city.

source.people: NO OFFICEHOLDER YET. Georgia's cities and towns elect their own officials, and no statewide roster of them has been read for this app; the card names the place and links nothing it has not verified. Recorded as gap ga-municipal-officeholders.
source.applies: Georgia — statewide. A point outside every city and town is unincorporated, which the card states.

layers.label: Police Station
layers.rank_note: nearest police stations by straight-line distance — a point layer, ranked with the other nearest-N layers

source.answers: The three nearest police stations to the point, by straight-line distance, with each one's address.

boundary.label: USGS The National Map — structures layer 53 (Police Stations), queried live at runtime by a bounding envelope through the paged loader. Public domain. Measured 2026-10-29: 826 points in Georgia's envelope, under the service's 2,000-record cap today, and paged anyway so that stops being a fact anyone has to re-check.

source.people: NO OFFICEHOLDER, AND NONE IS MISSING: a police station is a facility, not an elected district. Nobody is elected from one.
source.applies: Georgia — plus the border strip its envelope necessarily includes. A BUILDING, NOT A JURISDICTION: which agency answers at a given point is a service-area question this instance has not been researched for, so the card says where the nearest are and never who serves you. Nearest-three is a proximity fact, so for a reader near the state line the nearest one really may be in a neighbouring state, and the card's intro says these are straight-line distances.

anchor_point.note: Georgia State Capitol grounds, 206 Washington Street SW, Atlanta, Fulton County — the west side of the grounds, chosen 123 m from the line between House Districts 58 and 59, which runs east of the Capitol (the Capitol's own address point sits 51 m from it), measured 2026-10-29 against the shipped files

negative_point.note: Tallahassee, Florida, about 26 km south of the Georgia line — outside Georgia and outside every other instance in the fleet, and inside permalink_gate so the app answers the click and every shipped layer correctly returns nothing. Measured 2026-10-29: TIGERweb's state layer names Florida here (controls: the State Capitol returns Georgia, and a point in the open Gulf of Mexico returns no state), and none of the state's shipped boundary files contains it. FLORIDA AND ALABAMA ARE THE TWO NEIGHBOURS NO INSTANCE SERVES, so the change that makes Florida live moves this point into Alabama, the way Kentucky's go-live moved Indiana's.
